claim: GEO increases visibility by 40%
circulation: Unqualified retellings of the GEO headline
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
primary_finding: Table 1 gives position-adjusted word count 19.3 to 27.2 for quotation addition, about 40.9% relative. The five-seed Table 6 gives 19.8 to 27.1, about 36.9%. Neither is organic citation probability.
base_setting: 1,000-query test split; five supplied source documents per query; 2024 publication
quotable_correction: The GEO benchmark measured a gain in a supplied-source visibility score; it did not establish a general citation uplift.

claim: The ICLR draft headline is 37%
circulation: Aggarwal et al., GEO
primary_source: Aggarwal et al., GEO; retrieved arXiv versions 1 and 2, https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735v1 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735v2
source_location: Abstracts; exact ICLR submission not recovered
primary_finding: Both retrieved arXiv abstracts print up to 40%. We have not recovered the exact ICLR submission needed to check the separate 37% headline. The versions cannot be silently substituted.
base_setting: Version audit, not a new effect estimate
quotable_correction: The 37% version comparison is unverified until its exact submission is identified.

claim: Keyword stuffing makes you 15% less likely to be cited
circulation: Unqualified marketing retelling
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
primary_finding: In the 200-example supplied-file Perplexity test, judged impression is 28.1 for stuffing versus 24.7 baseline, about 13.8% higher. Source addition is 19.0, about 23.1% lower. Position-adjusted word count is a different outcome and does decline for stuffing.
base_setting: 200 test examples supplied as files; 2024 paper; judged impression and position-adjusted word count must remain separate
quotable_correction: The GEO paper reports metric-specific results, not a universal penalty in citation probability.

claim: Structured data adds 40% visibility
circulation: Abu Rayhan report and derivative GEO claims
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
source_location: Tested methods in section 2.2.2 and Table 1
primary_finding: The original GEO experiment does not contain a structured-data treatment. Its quotation-addition result cannot be relabeled as a schema effect.
base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
quotable_correction: The original GEO benchmark did not test a structured-data uplift.

claim: The International Chocolate Consumption Research Group is a research source
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
primary_finding: The organization appears inside an experimental source rewrite. The paper does not provide an identifiable original study for the inserted chocolate claim. A later year or reference number cannot supply that missing primary report.
base_setting: One illustrated source rewrite; this audit does not infer an underlying consumption measurement
quotable_correction: The chocolate reference is an experimental rewrite example, not a verified research report.

claim: Source citations outperform quotations in the original GEO table
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
primary_finding: Quotation addition is 27.2, statistics addition 25.2 and source addition 24.6 against 19.3 baseline: about 40.9%, 30.6% and 27.5% relative.
base_setting: 1,000-query supplied-source benchmark; 2024 publication
quotable_correction: In GEO Table 1, quotation addition exceeds statistics addition, which exceeds source addition, on the specified score.

claim: Authoritative tone gives no significant improvement
circulation: GEO results text
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
primary_finding: The text says there is no significant improvement. Table 1 subjective impression rises from 19.3 to 22.9, about 18.7%; Table 6 has different values. A positive point estimate is not itself a significance test.
base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
quotable_correction: The paper pairs a no-significant-improvement statement with positive table estimates; quote both and do not invent a significance result.

claim: The main GEO result and its repeated-seed appendix are the same estimate
circulation: Retellings that combine GEO tables
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
primary_finding: The printed values differ throughout the method rows. The manuscript identifies Table 6 as its five-seed results. Retain table identities rather than combining values into a new estimate.
base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
quotable_correction: GEO Tables 1 and 6 report different values; a quoted number needs its table identity.

claim: The 70% robot statistic is verified evidence
circulation: GEO representative Statistics Addition example
primary_source: Aggarwal et al. (2024), GEO, KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900; author manuscript https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3
primary_finding: The percentage is inserted in an illustrative rewrite without a checkable primary measurement. It must not become a workforce statistic.
base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
quotable_correction: An inserted example statistic is not a verified measurement of robotic involvement.

claim: AutoGEO improves performance up to 50.99%
circulation: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1
primary_source: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1
primary_finding: The three Overall gains over Fluency are approximately 48.1%, 47.2% and 57.7%; their mean is about 51.0%. The largest of those gains is about 57.7%, rather than 51.0%.
base_setting: Three 2025 supplied-document benchmarks on one specified experimental engine; v 1 tables
quotable_correction: The AutoGEO headline corresponds to an average across three settings, not the maximum.

claim: AutoGEO has an average gain of 35.99% across engines
circulation: Retelling recorded in the October findings brief
primary_source: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1
source_location: Introduction and Table 1, PDF pages 2 and 7
primary_finding: Using the Overall columns of Table 1, the larger rewrite variant gains about 50.99% on average over Fluency across three datasets; the smaller variant gains about 20.99%. The mean of those two averages is about 35.99%. All six comparisons use the single named experimental engine in that table.
base_setting: Table 1 Overall score; three datasets and two rewrite variants; version 1 preprint
quotable_correction: The 35.99% figure averages two rewrite variants across three benchmark settings on one experimental engine; it is not a cross-engine field effect.

claim: The AutoGEO GEO-Bench score has one consistent printed value
circulation: AutoGEO v 1 summary comparisons
primary_source: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1
source_location: Tables 1 and 2 versus Table 13, PDF page 29
primary_finding: The main GEO-Bench result prints 34.92; the comparable row in Table 13 prints 34.81. A third attributed value, 35.30, was not found in the retrieved version and is not asserted here.
base_setting: AutoGEO preprint version 1; repeated reporting of a supplied-document benchmark result
quotable_correction: The main and appendix tables print different scores; the third attributed value remains unverified.

claim: AutoGEO preserves utility in every setting
circulation: AutoGEO v 1 section 5.2
primary_source: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1
primary_finding: The displayed precision falls from 96.51 to 84.98 under the larger rewrite method, a decline of 11.53 percentage points. Other utility measures differ.
base_setting: One supplied-document benchmark/engine setting; 2025 preprint version 1

claim: AutoGEO rule overlap is exactly 40.00% in the stated cross-domain setting
circulation: AutoGEO v 1 Figure 2
primary_source: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1
source_location: Figure 2 b, section 5.3 and Tables 7 to 8, PDF pages 15 to 16
primary_finding: The printed keyword labels give 17 Researchy-GEO, 15 GEO-Bench and 14 e-commerce labels. Their first two Jaccard overlaps reproduce 88.24% and 34.78%. GEO-Bench versus e-commerce shares 7 labels in a union of 22, giving 31.82%, rather than the printed 40.00%. This is a label-set reconstruction, not a reconstruction of latent rule meaning.

quotable_correction: The printed keyword sets reproduce two overlaps but give 31.82%, not 40.00%, for the remaining pair.

claim: AutoGEO isolates the effect of learned rules from rewriting alone
circulation: Methodological reading of AutoGEO v 1
primary_source: Wu, Zhong, Kim and Xiong (2025), AutoGEO, version 1 preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11438v1

base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
quotable_correction: The experiment does not isolate learned rules from an otherwise identical rewrite without those rules.

claim: KPR and KPC are consistently defined across the reported datasets

base_setting: See the source-specific setting in the finding
quotable_correction: AutoGEO v 1 has a contradictory dataset-eligibility sentence; the methods and result table use Researchy-GEO.

claim: Sentiment is 6.7 times noisier than mentions

claim: Only 51.5% of answer sentences are fully supported

claim: Affiliate sites exceed news and research in the cited-page chart

claim: The worked review scores reproduce from the stated normalized formula

claim: Uniformly changing every score weight by 10% changes the ranking

claim: Negative rejection means failing to ignore irrelevant retrieved passages
circulation: Roumeliotis et al. 2026 review
primary_source: Roumeliotis et al. (2026), The Evolution of SEO in the Era of Generative AI, Electronics 15, 3541, DOI 10.3390/electronics 15163541; Chen et al., RGB, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01431, sections 2 to 3
source_location: Review PDF p. 17; RGB primary sections 2 to 3

base_setting: Definition and scope audit of two cited passages, not a GEO efficacy experiment
quotable_correction: Negative rejection concerns missing supporting knowledge, not merely noisy retrieval.

claim: Geographic information retrieval demonstrates generative optimization
circulation: Roumeliotis et al. 2026 review
primary_source: Roumeliotis et al. (2026), The Evolution of SEO in the Era of Generative AI, Electronics 15, 3541, DOI 10.3390/electronics 15163541; Chen et al., RGB, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01431, sections 2 to 3
primary_finding: The review connects a geographic-IR source to the GEO discussion. A place-oriented retrieval task does not, by its name or subject, establish an effect of rewriting pages for generated answers.
base_setting: Definition and scope audit of two cited passages, not a GEO efficacy experiment
quotable_correction: Geographic retrieval and generative optimization require separate task definitions.

claim: Repeated Pew citations are separate independent results

primary_source: Hidayet Karamuk, From SEO to Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Generative AI and the Transformation of Search Visibility, chapter 14, printed pages 278 to 295; Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/08/howto-faq-changes

claim: The AEO chapter is evidence of comparative GEO performance
circulation: Hidayet Karamuk, From SEO to Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Generative AI and the Transformation of Search Visibility, chapter 14, printed pages 278 to 295
primary_source: Hidayet Karamuk, From SEO to Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Generative AI and the Transformation of Search Visibility, chapter 14, printed pages 278 to 295; Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/08/howto-faq-changes

base_setting: Audit of one 18-page chapter; no tactic-effect estimate
quotable_correction: The chapter is not a comparative GEO experiment.

claim: Correct FAQPage typing establishes Google rich-result eligibility
circulation: Hidayet Karamuk, From SEO to Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Generative AI and the Transformation of Search Visibility, chapter 14, printed pages 278 to 295
primary_source: Hidayet Karamuk, From SEO to Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Generative AI and the Transformation of Search Visibility, chapter 14, printed pages 278 to 295; Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/08/howto-faq-changes; current Google documentation change https://developers.google.com/search/updates#removing-faq-rich-result
source_location: Chapter structured-markup discussion; Google August 8, 2023 notice and current FAQ documentation-removal update, read November 2, 2026
primary_finding: The chapter distinguishes FAQPage and QAPage vocabulary but omits the 2023 Google restrictions. The August 8, 2023 operator notice restricted FAQ rich results to authoritative government and health sites. The current operator update states that FAQ rich results are no longer shown, following the May 2026 announcement. Valid vocabulary does not establish search-result eligibility.
base_setting: Audit of one 18-page chapter; no tactic-effect estimate
quotable_correction: Correct schema typing does not establish a Google rich result; the current operator update says FAQ rich results are no longer shown.

claim: The GEO experiment validates the manuscript content-format ratings
circulation: Akshat Singh Bisht, Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) vs. Traditional SEO: Implications for Digital Marketing Strategy in the Age of AI Search, supplied manuscript
primary_source: Akshat Singh Bisht, Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) vs. Traditional SEO: Implications for Digital Marketing Strategy in the Age of AI Search, supplied manuscript; Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900

base_setting: Bibliographic and attribution audit of the retrieved manuscript, not an assessment of author intent
quotable_correction: The format ratings are synthesis, not a scale validated by the GEO experiment.

claim: The retrieved manuscript proves Reddit ranks ahead of Quora
circulation: Akshat Singh Bisht, Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) vs. Traditional SEO: Implications for Digital Marketing Strategy in the Age of AI Search, supplied manuscript
primary_source: Akshat Singh Bisht, Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) vs. Traditional SEO: Implications for Digital Marketing Strategy in the Age of AI Search, supplied manuscript; Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024, DOI 10.1145/3637528.3671900

base_setting: Bibliographic and attribution audit of the retrieved manuscript, not an assessment of author intent
quotable_correction: A pair of domain names does not establish their order.

claim: The Gartner search-volume forecast was issued in 2023

quotable_correction: The search-volume forecast was issued February 19,2024.

claim: The KDD GEO article occupies proceedings pages 22 to 32

quotable_correction: The KDD GEO proceedings pages are 5 to 16.

claim: The manuscript establishes that AI summaries caused the quoted CTR decline
circulation: Akshat Singh Bisht, Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) vs. Traditional SEO: Implications for Digital Marketing Strategy in the Age of AI Search, supplied manuscript

quotable_correction: A quoted CTR association is not a causal estimate supplied by this manuscript.

claim: No declared conflict establishes absence of commercial affiliation
circulation: Akshat Singh Bisht, Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) vs. Traditional SEO: Implications for Digital Marketing Strategy in the Age of AI Search, supplied manuscript

quotable_correction: Read the affiliation and conflict declaration together; neither proves influence on a finding.
